jobs.title: Director, Engineering, AI
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you passionate about transforming how legal professionals find trusted answers with AI? Join our Global Westlaw Engineering organization and help shape the future of AI-driven legal research.

Westlaw helps legal professionals around the world research, analyze, and act with confidence. We are building the next generation of fiduciary-level, AI-powered legal research and workflow capabilities, and we are changing how we build software.

As Director, you will lead a global organization of engineering managers, senior engineers, and vendor partners. You will own the multi-year AI engineering strategy and its alignment with the product delivery roadmap. You will move the organization to mission-based teams with clear ownership and accountability. You will also drive the shift to AI-assisted, agent-driven development and use engineering data to guide decisions and show results.

We want a technical leader with a track record of leading AI transformation, who leads by example, stays hands-on, keeps up with AI and engineering best practices, uses data to find what needs to change, and empowers teams to innovate across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Lead

Lead a high-performing global organization. Set clear expectations, coach managers and engineers, and lead by example, using AI tools and engineering data in your own work.
Stay close to the technical work. Work directly with senior engineers on architecture, technical direction, and hard problems to raise the technical bar across the organization.
Own Engineering strategy implementation and its alignment with the product delivery roadmap. Run it as a living plan with clear milestones and owners, adapt quickly as priorities evolve, and recommend measures that keep engineering objectives aligned to business strategy.
Lead the transformation to a mission-based operating model. Replace project-by-project handoffs with long-lived teams that own a product area, service, or customer outcome from design through production support. Define each team's mission, scope, decision rights, and the skills and authority it needs.
Set measures for each mission. Define measures such as reliability, quality, delivery speed, adoption, and cost. Review them regularly and use them to guide priorities, resourcing, and accountability.
Manage the vendor relationship. Help the vendor keep pace with business needs. Integrate vendor-managed teams into the organization, with clear scope, outcomes, service levels, and governance. Hold them to the same standards as internal teams for architecture, quality, security, and delivery, and measure their performance with the same data. Make sure they document their work and transfer knowledge, so the organization does not depend on a single vendor.
Decide what to do in-house, with partners, or through vendors. Balance cost, speed, capability, risk, and long-term knowledge retention.
Communicate proactively. Show how your organization's work delivers business value and supports strategy, and work directly with stakeholders and peers to shape the future of our products.

Deliver

Deliver strategic projects with urgency. Partner with Product Management, UX Design, and other Technology teams. Remove blockers, make timely decisions, and enable your teams to solve complex business problems with clearly defined outcomes.
Drive the end-to-end AI lifecycle. Own the work from retrieval and model integration through evaluation, deployment, and monitoring.
Set the standard for operational excellence. Hold AI and non-AI services to high standards for reliability, security, performance, and cost. Champion a DevOps-first model supported by automation, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code on AWS.
Manage the project portfolio. Own budget, priorities, and staff allocation.

Operate: Run a Data-Driven, AI-Enabled Organization:

Provide guardrails and empower teams to use AI. Equip managers, engineers, and teams to apply AI in daily engineering work, including coding assistants, agents, code review, test automation, and quality evaluation. Provide clear guardrails for responsible use, covering security, data handling, and human review of AI-generated code and outputs. Within those guardrails, encourage teams to experiment and adopt AI, and remove the barriers that slow them down.
Make decisions with data. Analyze GitHub data, such as pull request cycle time, review latency, build and deployment frequency, and AI tool usage, to find bottlenecks and show where change is working.
Track ownership and accountability. Use incident response, change failure rate, and cycle time by team to show whether ownership and accountability are improving. Share results openly, use them to coach rather than blame, and turn them into practical changes in how teams work.
Measure the impact of AI. Track its effect on delivery speed, code quality, defect rates, and reliability. Use those measures to adjust strategy and investment.
Own the economics of AI usage. Set AI budgets, and track and optimize token consumption, inference cost, and tooling spend. Guide model selection and cost-versus-quality trade-offs, balancing them against productivity, quality, and speed.

Innovate

Stay on top of the AI landscape. Follow new models, agent frameworks, tool protocols such as MCP, and retrieval patterns. Judge what is production-ready, bring it into your teams' practices, and grow adoption of AI/ML engineering practices and frameworks across the enterprise.
Try new approaches. Take informed risks. Encourage your managers and teams to do the same, and recognize those who do.

Required Qualifications

Education. A bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience. 10+ years in software development, including 3+ years leading AI solution development, and 10+ years managing managers and building high-performing engineering teams in an agile environment.
Organizational leadership. Experience leading managers, individual contributors, and vendor-managed teams, including scope, performance, cost, and quality. You can coach managers on people leadership and engage credibly with Staff and Principal engineers.
Strategy and execution. Experience turning a multi-year vision into programs, roadmaps, and measurable results across multiple teams, including large-scale rollouts and infrastructure initiatives.
Shipping AI in production. A track record of shipping LLM-based applications, RAG, or agent workflows in production-grade software. You can speak credibly about prompt and context design, retrieval, evaluation, and production trade-offs.
Cloud, DevOps, and reliability. Strong depth in cloud-native architecture on AWS, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code, and experience running mission-critical, high-availability systems.
Hands-on AI tool use. Daily use of AI coding tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code). You lead by example and have empowered managers and teams to adopt AI-assisted development, with strong practices for review, quality, and security.
Data-driven leadership and AI economics. Experience defining and analyzing metrics such as DORA, cycle time, quality, and adoption to find problems and show results. Working knowledge of token usage, inference and tooling costs, and how to measure the return on AI investment.
Leading change. Experience shifting team mindsets, introducing new tools and ways of working, and moving teams to mission-based, outcome-owned models with clear ownership, decision rights, and accountability.
Communication. Excellent communication skills. You can explain complex technical and financial trade-offs to executives and customers and align stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading globally distributed teams and restructuring an engineering organization around products, services, or customer outcomes.
Agentic systems and responsible AI. Experience shipping agentic systems in production, including evaluation, benchmarking, and monitoring, and knowledge of AI guardrails and governance.
LLM APIs, search, and agent frameworks. Experience with LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) at scale, information retrieval or search systems, and standards such as Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Vendor and cost management. Experience with vendor selection, contract negotiation, and transitions between vendor and in-house teams. Experience managing cloud and AI cost through FinOps or inference cost optimization.
Career paths. Experience building career paths for both management and technical (IC) tracks, and retaining senior technical talent.
Technical background. Strong Python and RESTful API design skills. AWS certifications, such as Solutions Architect or DevOps Engineer, are a plus.
Domain background. Background in legal or other regulated, content-rich professional domains.

This posting is for proactive recruitment purposes and may be used to fill current openings or future vacancies within our organization.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.
Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.
Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

The AI system acts as a supporting tool, but there is always a human making the decision if you will be considered for the role.

jobs.title: Strategy Director, Catalyst Team
jobs.description:
Who are we?

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.

A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.

Job Summary

The Business Operations Catalyst team is Equinix’s internal consulting and sprint execution engine, partnering directly with senior leaders to solve the company’s most complex, high-impact enterprise problems. Catalyst engagements typically run 3-6 months, rapidly mobilizing cross-functional teams to drive clarity, decisions, and actionable execution plans before transitioning ownership to the long-term business owner.

A Catalyst Strategy Director is a senior, business-facing leader who leads 1-3 initiatives simultaneously from problem definition through execution. This role partners closely with executive leadership to frame complex decisions, synthesize insights into clear recommendations, and ensure programs deliver measurable business outcomes.  You serve as the primary driver, integrator and facilitator, guiding senior leaders through ambiguity, trade-offs, and critical decisions while ensuring work remains enterprise-aligned, actionable, and outcome-driven.

This role requires expert synthesis capabilities, strong executive presence, and the ability to quickly connect dots across strategy and execution – setting the standard for how Catalyst engagements are run.

Responsibilities

Impact‑Oriented Problem Solving and Decision Making

Frame and structure complex, ambiguous programs and engagements, rapidly identifying critical issues, priorities, and interdependencies.
Synthesize data, insights, and stakeholder perspectives into clear, actionable decision options.
Guide teams to apply the most appropriate problem-solving techniques. Own, oversee and challenge analytical work (e.g., financial, headcount, operational models) to ensure rigor, root‑cause clarity, and sound judgment.
Advise senior leaders on risks, implications, and downstream impacts, balancing strategy, execution realities, and enterprise considerations.

Adaptable Leadership and Facilitation

Facilitate high‑stakes, cross‑functional, and executive decision‑making forums, including E‑Team discussions.
Set the standard for facilitation and decision framing – ensuring options are enterprise‑consistent, decisive, and clearly communicated.
Operate effectively in high‑pressure, emotionally charged environments with a solution‑oriented, enterprise mindset.
Manage escalations in partnership with executive sponsors, treating setbacks as opportunities for progress.
Coach and mentor more junior Catalyst team members, strengthening problem‑solving, facilitation, and leadership capability across the team.

Synthesis and Strategic Communication

Clearly understands and communicates the vision and objectives of the engagement, providing clear day-to-day direction to the team and business leads
Own engagement framing and alignment with initiative leadership and executive sponsors. 
Connect disparate inputs and synthesize complexity in real-time, driving clarity, alignment and momentum.
Communicate difficult messages constructively; listen actively and accurately reflect stakeholder perspectives.
Distill complexity into clear insights, structured narratives, and compelling recommendations.

Program Ownership & Execution

Lead multiple complex, multi‑workstream Catalyst programs concurrently, maintaining quality, consistency, and pace. 
Establish appropriate governance, operating models, escalation paths, and decision forums.
Translate strategic intent into sequenced, prioritized execution plans that convert decisions into sustained action.
Own core program artifacts including charters, RAID logs, integrated project plans, and operating cadences.
Design and implement repeatable frameworks, templates, and governance mechanisms that strengthen the Catalyst operating model.
Partner with Change and Communications teams to embed change strategy and proactively mitigate adoption risks.

Trusted Partnership

Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the E‑Team and senior leaders, influencing decisions through judgment, discretion, and insight.
Build rapid command of the business and educate leaders on trade‑offs, implications, and recommendations.
Model and reinforce an enterprise mindset across all engagements.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will demonstrate the following attributes:

8+ years of relevant experience; with management consulting or internal consulting experience
Proven success leading complex, cross‑functional initiatives with senior executives
Exceptional problem‑solving, analytical, and synthesis skills
Quick learner and ability to think on your feet
Strong executive presence and communication skills
High emotional intelligence and ability to influence
Highly skilled in navigating ambiguity
Ability to pivot between the big picture and the details
Tenacity, resilience, and a results‑driven mindset
Proven experience in program and project management

The targeted pay range for this position in the following location is / locations are:

Canada - Toronto Office TRO : 166,000 - 248,000 CAD / Annual

Our pay ranges reflect the minimum and maximum target for new hire pay for the full-time position determined by role, level, and location. The pay range shown is based on our compensation structure in place at the time of posting and may be updated periodically based on business needs.
Individual pay is based on additional factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education and/or training.

The targeted pay range listed reflects the base pay only and does not include bonus, equity, or benefits. Employees are eligible for bonus, and equity may be offered depending on the position.

Equinix Benefits

As an employee, you become important to Equinix’s success. We ensure all your benefits are in line with our core values: competitive, inclusive, sustainable, connected and efficient. We keep them competitive within the current marketplace to ensure we’re providing you with the best package possible. So, wherever you are in your career and life, you’ll be able to enhance your experience and bring your whole self to work.

Employee Assistance Program
: An Employee Assistance program is available to all employees.

Canada Core Benefits: - Insurance: You may enroll in healthcare coverage that is designed to complement the provincial healthcare system, along with life, disability and optional benefit plans that are designed for you and your eligible family members. - Retirement: You may also enroll in Equinix-sponsored retirement or savings plans: Defined Contribution Pension Plan (DCPP), Group Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) and Tax-Free Savings Plan (TSFA). - Vacation and Paid Holidays: Equinix offers both vacation and personal time, along with various paid holidays for you to rest and recharge. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits. Benefits are subject to specific plan or program terms, and to change at Equinix discretion.

Equinix is committed to ensuring that our employment process is open to all individuals, including those with a disability. If you are a qualified candidate and need assistance or an accommodation, please let us know by completing this form.

Equinix is an Equal Employment Opportunity and, in the U.S., an Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to unlawful consideration of race, color, religion, creed, national or ethnic origin, ancestry, place of birth, citizenship, sex, pregnancy / childbirth or related medical conditions, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or domestic partnership status, age, veteran or military status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, political / organizational affiliation, status as a victim or family member of a victim of crime or abuse, or any other status protected by applicable law.
